extracted.intended_audience: students of algebraic topology / readers studying singular homology (undergraduate/graduate level)
extracted.subtask_description: Definitions, algebraic properties, and computational tools for singular homology: chain complexes, homology groups, functoriality, long exact sequences, Mayer–Vietoris, reduced and relative homology, and example computations (spheres, torus, figure eight).

rubrics_metrics.name: Chain complex condition
rubrics_metrics.description: A chain complex is a sequence of groups A_n and maps ... → A_{n+1} ∂→ A_n ∂→ A_{n-1} → ... such that the composition of any two adjacent maps is the zero morphism (i.e. ∂∘∂ = 0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This algebraic abstraction (denoted A_•) is the foundation for defining homology in any category (not just Ab). The nth homology H_n(A_•) is ker(A_n → A_{n-1}) / im(A_{n+1} → A_n).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of nth homology group
rubrics_metrics.description: For a topological space X, H_n(X) is defined as Z_n(X) / B_n(X) where Z_n(X)=ker(∂: C_n(X)→C_{n-1}(X)) (cycles) and B_n(X)=im(∂: C_{n+1}(X)→C_n(X)) (boundaries).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretation: cycles are chains with zero boundary; boundaries are those chains that are boundaries of higher-dimensional chains; homology measures cycles modulo boundaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bn and Zn are subgroups and inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: B_n and Z_n are themselves abelian groups, with B_n(X) ⊆ Z_n(X) ⊆ C_n(X).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check basic algebraic properties: closure under addition and inverses; inclusion follows from ∂∘∂=0 so im ∂ ⊆ ker ∂.

rubrics_metrics.name: Zeroth homology detects path components
rubrics_metrics.description: H_0(X) corresponds to path-connected components: if X has r path-connected components then H_0(X) ≅ Z^{⊕ r}. In particular, if X is path-connected then H_0(X) ≅ Z.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intuition: points are 0-simplices, every point is a cycle; boundaries identify points connected by paths (so components give summands).

rubrics_metrics.name: Homology splits over path-connected components
rubrics_metrics.description: If X = ⨆_α X_α is decomposition into path-connected components then H_n(X) ≅ ⊕_α H_n(X_α).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Homology respects disjoint unions (direct sums) because chain groups split accordingly; treat abelian groups as Z-modules so use ⊕ notation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hurewicz theorem (n=1 special statement)
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is path-connected then H_1(X) is the abelianization of π_1(X, x_0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rough explanation: 1-cycles correspond to loops; B_1 are null-homotopic loops; H_1 allows loops to commute (abelianization of π_1). (Full Hurewicz proved elsewhere.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Functoriality of homology
rubrics_metrics.description: For fixed n, H_n is a functor hTop → Ab: a continuous map f:X→Y induces f_*:H_n(X)→H_n(Y); homotopic maps induce the same map on homology; homotopy equivalences induce isomorphisms on homology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction of f_* is via the induced chain map C_n(X)→C_n(Y). Show independence of homotopy via chain homotopy (more delicate than π_1 case).

rubrics_metrics.name: Chain map induces homology map
rubrics_metrics.description: A morphism of chain complexes (chain map) f:A_•→B_• (a sequence of maps commuting with ∂) sends cycles to cycles and boundaries to boundaries, hence induces maps f_*:H_n(A_•)→H_n(B_•).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diagram commutativity ensures well-definedness on homology; view chain complexes as category Cmplx and H_n as a functor Cmplx→Grp.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chain homotopy definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Two chain maps f,g:A_•→B_• are chain homotopic if there exist maps P_n:A_n→B_{n+1} with g_n − f_n = ∂_B∘P_n + P_{n-1}∘∂_A for every n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Picture: the slanted dotted arrows (P_n) give 'parallelograms' where g−f equals the sum of the two side compositions. This algebraic notion models topological homotopy at chain level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chain homotopic maps induce same homology map
rubrics_metrics.description: If f and g are chain homotopic, then the induced maps f_*, g_* : H_n(A_•) → H_n(B_•) coincide for each n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof idea: show g−f sends cycles to boundaries in B, so g_* − f_* = 0 on homology. Exercise: verify every cycle of A_n becomes a boundary under g−f.

rubrics_metrics.name: Map of spaces induces chain map (prism construction)
rubrics_metrics.description: A continuous map f:X→Y induces maps C_n(X)→C_n(Y) by composing singular simplices with f. If f and g are homotopic, one can construct a chain homotopy between the induced chain maps using the prism operator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Geometric construction: use homotopy F:X×[0,1]→Y and subdivide Δ^n×[0,1] into n+1 simplices; define P_n(ϕ)=∑_{i=0}^n (−1)^i (F∘(ϕ×id)) [v_0,...,v_i,w_i,...,w_n]. Identity: ∂_Y(P_n(σ)) = g(σ) − f(σ) − P_{n-1}(∂_X σ).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduced homology (augmentation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Augment the singular chain complex by adding ε:C_0(X)→Z (ε(∑ n_i p_i)=∑ n_i) to obtain the augmented complex eC_•(X). The reduced homology eH_n(X) is the homology of this augmented complex.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relations: eH_n(X) ≅ H_n(X) for n>0; H_0(X) ≅ eH_0(X) ⊕ Z. For contractible X, all reduced homology groups vanish. Interpretation uses a (−1)-simplex (the empty simplex) generating C_{−1} ≅ Z.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative chain groups and relative homology
rubrics_metrics.description: For A ⊆ X define C_n(X,A):=C_n(X)/C_n(A). The boundary operator descends, yielding the relative chain complex whose homology groups are H_n(X,A).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intuition: chains supported in A are trivial. Beware naive equalities: H_n(X,A) ≠ H_n(X)/H_n(A) in general. Often H_n(X,A) ≅ eH_n(X/A) for 'reasonable' pairs (discussed later), but counterexamples exist when quotients are pathological.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mayer–Vietoris short exact sequence (chain-level)
rubrics_metrics.description: For an open cover X=U∪V define C_n(U+V) as chains with simplices entirely in U or V. There is a short exact sequence 0 → C_•(U∩V) → C_•(U)⊕C_•(V) → C_•(U+V) → 0 (map c ↦ (c,−c), (c,d)↦c+d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Augmenting gives 0→eC_•(U∩V)→eC_•(U)⊕eC_•(V)→eC_•(U+V)→0. The short exactness is checked by basis arguments (kernel equals image).

rubrics_metrics.name: Short exact sequences give long exact sequences in homology
rubrics_metrics.description: Given 0→A_•→B_•→C_•→0 short exact sequence of chain complexes, there is an induced long exact sequence ...→H_n(A_•)→H_n(B_•)→H_n(C_•)→H_{n-1}(A_•)→... with connecting homomorphisms ∂:H_n(C_•)→H_{n-1}(A_•).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof via diagram chase (or snake lemma). The connecting map ∂ is constructed by lifting a cycle in C_n to B_n, applying ∂_B, and pulling back to A_{n-1} (the 'left, down, left' recipe); check well-definedness carefully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long exact sequence for relative homology
rubrics_metrics.description: For A ⊆ X there is a long exact sequence ...→H_n(A)→H_n(X)→H_n(X,A)→H_{n-1}(A)→... (and a reduced version).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This sequence comes from the short exact sequence 0→C_•(A)→C_•(X)→C_•(X,A)→0 and is a primary computational tool for relating absolute and relative homology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open cover homology theorem (identifying C_•(U+V) with C_•(X))
rubrics_metrics.description: For X=U∪V (open cover) the inclusion ι:C_•(U+V)→C_•(X) induces isomorphism H_n(U+V) ≅ H_n(X).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thus the Mayer–Vietoris long exact sequence can be realized with H_n(X) in place of H_n(U+V). Remark: true for arbitrary open covers (even uncountable), though only two-set case is usually stated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computation of homology of spheres
rubrics_metrics.description: Reduced homology of the m-sphere: eH_n(S^m) ≅ Z if n=m and 0 otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof via Mayer–Vietoris by splitting S^m into two hemispheres (contractible) whose intersection is homotopy equivalent to S^{m−1}. The connecting homomorphism supplies the generator for the top homology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mayer–Vietoris computational strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Mayer–Vietoris lets one compute H_n(X) by splitting X into two open sets U and V and using the long exact sequence relating H_n(U∩V), H_n(U)⊕H_n(V), and H_n(X).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical tactic: choose U,V with simpler homology (often contractible or known), analyze connecting maps, and deduce H_n(X); sometimes must compute the maps explicitly (e.g. torus example).

rubrics_metrics.name: Splitting lemma for short exact sequences
rubrics_metrics.description: For 0→A→^f B→^g C→0 of abelian groups the following are equivalent: (a) there exists p:B→A with p∘f = id_A; (b) there exists s:C→B with g∘s = id_C; (c) B ≅ A⊕C making diagram commute. In particular, (b) holds when C is free.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequences: when a short exact sequence splits, B is determined as direct sum of A and C. Example of non-splitting: 0→Z/2 →^{×2} Z/4 ↠ Z/2 →0 (Z/4 ≄ Z/2⊕Z/2). Valid in any abelian category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caveats about quotient and relative homology / pathological examples
rubrics_metrics.description: While often H_n(X,A) ≅ eH_n(X/A), counterexamples exist when A is not closed or X/A is pathological (e.g. non-Hausdorff or spaces with infinite behavior).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: If A=X\{0} in disk D^2, H_2(X,A) ≅ Z but H_2(X/A) ≅ 0. The 'shrinking wedge' example shows q_*:H_1(X,A)→H_1(X/A) need not be injective; intuition: algebraic chains are finite while quotient can involve infinitely many loops.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exactness definitions and short exact sequence characterizations
rubrics_metrics.description: A sequence ...→G_{n+1}→G_n→G_{n-1}→... is exact if im of any arrow equals kernel of next arrow. 0→A→B is exact iff A→B is injective; A→B→0 is exact iff A→B is surjective; short exact sequences are 0→A→B→C→0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understanding exactness is essential for manipulating sequences and applying diagram chases producing long exact sequences in homology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of explicit chain-level maps to compute kernels/images
rubrics_metrics.description: Computations (e.g. torus) may require understanding explicit induced maps on homology arising from chain-level maps (e.g. inclusion map C_•(U∩V)→C_•(U)⊕C_•(V) is c↦(c,−c), inducing ϕ on homology).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In examples, analyze images/kernels of these induced maps as matrices on Z-summands to determine H_n(X) (e.g. deduce eH_2(T^2)≅Z via kernel of ϕ generated by z1−z2).
